sections.h2: How Johns Creek owners usually sell
sections.html:
Most go through a broker listing, some negotiate directly with a buyer, and a smaller group takes an investor's cash bid. The deciding factors are the calendar and the shape of the house. Johns Creek lies in northeastern Fulton County, so the tax bills and recording steps involve Fulton County as well as the city.

A broker listing fits a house that photographs well, since it reaches the biggest group of buyers, at the price of staging, inspections and a lender's appraisal. Negotiating directly saves the commission and hands every task to you. An investor's cash bid gives up price in return for speed and certainty.

  • Highest price: a prepared listing, ideally with a broker who knows your subdivision and school zone.
  • Most control: a direct sale, if contracts and disclosures do not worry you.
  • Fastest or easiest: an investor bid on a house with condition problems.

Whatever you choose, assemble the deed, the newest Fulton County tax bill, any homeowner association papers and the permits for work done on the house. Permit history is easy to retrieve because the city issues permits through an online portal.

The 2025 estimate for Johns Creek is 80,401 people, and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners, 80.4 percent for 2020-2024. The midpoint home value is $629,400.

With that many owner-occupied homes, a typical Johns Creek sale is one resident handing a lived-in house to another family. Households average 2.82 people, so the family-sized house is the usual comparison.

Johns Creek incorporated on December 1, 2006, and covers about 32 square miles roughly 25 miles north of Atlanta. Recreation and Parks maintains more than 400 acres of parkland and nature reserve, with five access points to the Chattahoochee River.

  • Mail can carry a Johns Creek address with any of five ZIP codes: 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 or 30097.
  • The city does not run garbage collection, so residents contract with private haulers.
  • Water comes through Fulton County, and power through Georgia Power or Sawnee Electric.
  • Police and fire service come from the city's own departments.

Have those answers ready. A mailing address can carry a neighboring city's name, so buyers should confirm the property is inside Johns Creek with the city's address tool.

Fulton County Schools serves Johns Creek, and 19 of its public elementary, middle and high schools serve residents. Which one a child attends depends on the address and the attendance zone.

Eleven Fulton County elementary schools and one charter school serve the city, with names such as Abbotts Hill, Barnwell, Dolvin, Findley Oaks, Medlock Bridge, Ocee, Shakerag, State Bridge Crossing and Wilson Creek. Some of the elementary schools carry Roswell or Alpharetta mailing addresses even though they serve Johns Creek families. Four private schools also serve the city: Holy Redeemer Catholic School, Mount Pisgah Christian School, Perimeter School and Woodward Academy North.

Zoning is address-specific, so do not tell a buyer which school a house feeds without checking. Direct buyers to Fulton County Schools to confirm the current zone for the exact address.

sections.h2: Where a Johns Creek tax bill comes from
sections.html:
Johns Creek owners owe tax to Fulton County, which includes the school system, and to the City of Johns Creek. The Fulton County Tax Commissioner mails the bill.

The Fulton County Board of Assessors sets the value and mails the Notice of Assessment each year. The notice prints the appeal deadline, so read it as soon as it arrives. Homeowners who qualify for a homestead exemption but miss the April 1 filing date can still apply during the appeal period, and anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year. Each notice now shows estimated tax savings, with discounts and exemptions, in place of an estimated tax figure.

  • Search your parcel on the Fulton assessor's site to verify the exemptions on record.
  • Ask the Fulton County Tax Commissioner whether the current bill is paid.
  • Have your closing attorney show how this year's tax is shared with the new owner.

Johns Creek runs building permits through an online customer self-service portal, and its permit process has six steps: application, fee payment, plan review, permit issued, required inspections and permit completed. The city also posts a Do I Need a Permit checklist.

If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a major system without a permit, a buyer's inspection may find it. The city's Code Compliance Division enforces the local ordinances and property maintenance code, and the nuisance and zoning ordinances are posted on its code regulations page. Ask Community Development whether any permit on your address is still open and close it out before you list.

Recording the deed also triggers Georgia's transfer tax. Check the contract to see which side pays.

sections.h2: Steps from accepted offer to closing
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, a title search confirms who owns the house and whether any liens remain. Your closing attorney prepares a settlement statement showing the payoff, the shared tax and any fees. The buyer pays by wire or by lender funding, and the deed is recorded in Fulton County.

With a cash buyer, the lender's appraisal and underwriting drop out of the sequence, which is where most delay comes from in a financed sale. With a financed buyer, expect an inspection and an appraisal, and either can bring a request to lower the price. Keep permit records and receipts for major work in one folder so questions get quick answers.

sections.h2: When an investor's bid makes sense
sections.html:
An investor's bid is worth a look when you cannot or will not prepare the house for retail buyers. Houses here carry high values, and a dated or damaged one can sit while carrying costs keep running.

  • An estate house whose heirs live elsewhere.
  • Deferred maintenance that would not survive a buyer's inspection.
  • A relocation with a short fuse.
  • Past work done without a permit.

Request any bid in writing, see which closing charges are yours, and set it beside a listing broker's net estimate.

faqs.q: Do Johns Creek owners pay both city and county tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Fulton County, including the school system, and the City of Johns Creek each tax the property, and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner sends the bill.

faqs.q: Is a Johns Creek mailing address always inside the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Johns Creek shares the ZIP codes 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 and 30097 with neighboring cities, and the city offers an address lookup tool for confirmation.

faqs.q: Who hauls trash at a Johns Creek house?
faqs.a: A private company does. The city provides no garbage collection, so residents contract on their own, and a buyer will ask which hauler serves the house.

faqs.q: Can I still file for a Fulton County homestead exemption after April 1?
faqs.a: Owners who qualify but missed April 1 can apply during the appeal period printed on the notice. Anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Which side pays Georgia's transfer tax on a Johns Creek sale?
faqs.a: State law makes the seller liable, though contracts often move the cost to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded.
